cards.text: This psalm doesn't say who wrote it, but the psalmist opens LOUD, calling to the righteous: "Rejoice in the LORD, O righteous ones". No name on it, like a cookie box left on your porch with no card. Friend, you don't need a card to know that box is GOOD.

cards.question: The psalmist opens by calling out to the righteous ones. He says it is fitting for the upright to ___ Him.

cards.text: Then the psalmist starts handing out the music: the harp, ten strings, and a new song to sing to the LORD. Friend, I play ZERO strings, so in this band I'm the guy carrying the harp in from the car.

cards.question: The psalmist calls for harps, ten strings and a new song for the LORD. True or false: He wants this new song played quietly with no shouting.

cards.text: So why the band and the shouting? Because "the word of the LORD is upright", and friend, when I say a batch will be ready in five minutes, that's not upright, that's a WISH.

cards.question: The word of the LORD is upright. True or false: The psalmist says some of the LORD's work can't be trusted.

cards.text: Then the psalmist tells us what the LORD loves: righteousness and justice. He doesn't just like them, baker. He LOVES them.

cards.question: The LORD loves righteousness and justice. Looking at the whole earth, what does the psalmist say it's full of?

cards.text: Then the psalmist goes way back: by the word of the LORD the heavens were made. No mixer, no measuring cups, and meanwhile I need three bowls and a prayer just to get one batch out.

cards.question: The heavens were made by the word of the LORD. What does the psalmist say all the stars were made by?

cards.text: He piles up the waters of the sea and puts the depths into storehouses. Baker, I spill ONE cup of flour in my bakery and it takes me all afternoon to sweep it up.

cards.question: The seas piled up and the stars made by His breath. Then the psalmist calls for a response. True or false: He says only the people of Israel should fear the LORD.
The psalmist wants all the people of the world to revere the LORD. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He spoke and it came to be
He worked and it was built
He waited and it took shape

cards.text: Then the psalmist turns to the nations: the LORD frustrates their plans and thwarts the devices of the peoples. Friend, I plan a perfect batch every morning, and my oven has OTHER plans.

cards.question: The nations' plans get frustrated. But the psalmist says the counsel of the LORD stands ___.

cards.text: And the purposes of His heart go on to all generations. Friend, MY purposes last until about my afternoon nap.
The nations' plans get frustrated. But now the psalmist names a nation that IS blessed.

cards.question: The psalmist says one nation is blessed. Which one?

answers.text: The nation whose God is the LORD
The nation with the largest army
The nation with the richest king

cards.text: They're the people He has chosen as His inheritance! Friend, I got picked out of a bakery's closing-sale bin for 25 cents, so believe me, being chosen is a BIG deal.

cards.question: The LORD looks down from heaven. Who does the psalmist say He sees?

cards.text: From His dwelling place He gazes on all who live on the earth, and He shapes the hearts of each one. Nobody's stuck in the back of a junk drawer where He can't see them.

cards.question: The LORD shapes the hearts of each person. True or false: The psalmist says He pays no attention to what they do.
Next the psalmist looks at a king with a vast army. True or false: He says the king is saved by that army.

cards.text: And no warrior is delivered by his great strength either. Then the psalmist points at the horse, with all its great strength.

cards.question: When it comes to being saved, what does the psalmist call a horse?

cards.text: Even its great strength cannot save. Friend, this mustache can lift a FULL cookie box, and it never once lifted me out of that junk drawer.

cards.question: Armies, strength and horses can't save. But the eyes of the LORD are on those who ___ Him and whose ___ is in His loving devotion.
The LORD keeps His eyes on those who hope in His loving devotion. What for?

answers.text: To test their faith in Him

cards.text: And He keeps them alive in famine, when food runs short. Not just in the good seasons, friend, but in the lean ones too.
Now the psalm gets personal: "Our soul waits for the LORD". Friend, waiting is my WORST baking skill, because I stand at the oven window like staring makes it bake faster.

cards.question: The LORD delivers from death and keeps His people alive in famine. While their soul waits for Him, what does the psalmist call the LORD?
True or false: The psalmist says their hearts rejoice in the LORD because they trust in His holy name.

cards.text: And the psalm ends with a prayer straight to the LORD: "May Your loving devotion rest on us, O LORD, as we put our hope in You." It started with harps and shouting, and it lands right here, hoping in Him.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen final word of the BSB line. The earlier call to rejoice does not rule out obey or serve as fitting responses, so the baker must know or guess the verse's wording rather than reason out its meaning from the cards.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
